issues.description: The template file declares a class named AnimalFarm (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) instead of the expected Farm class described in the problem UML and implemented in the solution. This class-name mismatch prevents students from implementing or using the Farm API as specified (e.g., Main and tests expect a class named Farm with methods like addAnimal, singFarmSong, feedAllAnimals).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template from AnimalFarm to Farm and ensure its public API (constructors and methods) matches the UML and solution (addAnimal, singFarmSong, feedAllAnimals, getter/setter for animals). Provide the correct class declaration and remove the AnimalFarm name to align template with the specification.

issues.description: The template Farm.java file contains invalid and duplicated Java code (a nested 'package' declaration and a duplicated class body inside the singFarmSong method), causing syntax errors and making the template uncompilable. This structural corruption prevents students from being able to compile and run the project or follow the exercise scaffolding.
issues.suggestedFix: Clean up the template Farm.java so it contains a single valid public class declaration (Farm) and no nested package declarations or duplicated class definitions. Ensure methods like singFarmSong and singFarmSongVerse are declared at class level (not nested) and that the file compiles as-is to serve as a proper starter file.

issues.description: The template repository is missing the foundational classes and interfaces required by the problem (Animal abstract class, Rideable and Milkable interfaces, and concrete animal classes Seal, Pig, Goat). The problem statement and UML reference these types, and the solution provides them, but the template does not include stubs for students to implement, creating a gap between the specified design and the provided starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the required class and interface stubs to the template repository: an abstract Animal class with name field and getter/setter and abstract messageOnFeed(), interfaces Rideable and Milkable with the correct method signatures, and empty concrete classes Seal, Pig, and Goat extending/implementing the appropriate types. Ensure the filenames and packages match the problem specification so students can implement the bodies without having to create foundational types themselves.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a class named 'Farm', but the template file template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares the class as 'AnimalFarm'. This mismatch (file named Farm.java containing public class AnimalFarm) breaks the direct mapping students must make from the exercise description to the starter code and will cause confusion and compile errors when the rest of the template and tests refer to 'Farm'.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class declared in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (public class Farm) so the class name matches the filename, the problem statement, and the solution. Update any references in the template (e.g., Main.java) if necessary to refer to 'Farm'.
